segments.text: How does diesel fuel ignite the instant it meets hot air?
Atomised diesel is injected directly into the already super‑heated, compressed air during the combustion stroke.
Because the air temperature exceeds the fuel’s ignition point, the droplets flash into flame on contact.
The amount you inject decides the air‑fuel ratio, which directly controls torque.
Diesel engines vary power by changing fuel quantity, not by throttling intake air.
This means the intake stays fully open, letting the cylinder breathe freely.
The result is strong torque without a throttle plate.
So the instant spark‑free ignition happens because fuel meets hot air.
